body.estimand_functional:
Unconditionally on the exact-uniform class,
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
\gtrsim R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]
For the Kennedy-Theorem-1 slice,
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}
\gtrsim
\left\{n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\vee
n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/(\alpha+\beta))}\right\}
\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]
Only conditional on an affirmative resolution of Open-ended Question~1 does the exact-uniform relation strengthen to
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]

sampling_model.units: The observed records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with unknown Hölder propensity \(\pi\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The proposed target-fiber mechanism profiles over the full propensity and control-regression Hölder classes; no named nuisance estimator and no fixed finite nuisance sieve is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem~1 gives the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE lower bound on a class whose covariate density is bounded above; Theorem~2 treats attainability under separate estimator and design conditions.
Section~4 uses treated--control occupancy and effect homogeneity to obtain a global nonprivate rate with a collision term.
The paper stabilizes central-private U-statistics using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Section~4 gives a general pure-private T-mechanism based on clipped likelihood-ratio tests and finite covers.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad inequalities based on expected Hamming transport.
Theorems~1 and~3 give finite-query and functional observational CATE releases under approximate differential privacy.
The sparse-histogram lower bound and compact dense-histogram theorem show that pure-private costs can change with representation and occupancy.
Their multiscale and adaptive-lower-bound arguments are templates for the separate unresolved adaptation question; no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty is imported here.
The paper establishes nonprivate heterogeneous-effect minimax rates with explicit random-design geometry.
Definition~2 and Section~4 construct T-estimators from coherent tests on countable model nets.

body.tldr: The occupancy-weighted score has an unconditional exact expectation and constant replacement sensitivity, while the exact-uniform Hölder class has unconditional dense \(\rho_G\) and sparse \(\rho_F\) pure-private lower branches in addition to its nonprivate minimax floor.  Because the exact-uniform class is contained in the common-support/constants slice of Kennedy et al.'s Theorem~1 lower-bound class, all of these lower branches transfer upward and yield an explicit superclass converse.  A matching upper bound remains conditional on the unresolved full-fiber occupancy lift on the exact-uniform class, and smoothness adaptation remains wholly open; no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty is claimed.

project_justification.gap: No located result gives a pure-central-DP minimax frontier for pointwise CATE with unknown smooth propensity and outcome regression. The closest banked construction uses only exactly-two-record cells and therefore loses all signal when cell occupancy diverges.
project_justification.niche: Realized cell occupancy can amplify a degenerate nuisance-product signal while preserving constant record influence, potentially joining the sparse \(n^2\epsilon\) branch to the dense \(n\epsilon\) branch with no third radius.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the occupancy identity and the sparse and dense pure-private lower branches unconditionally on the exact-uniform class, then transfers the resulting converse upward to the Kennedy-Theorem-1 bounded-above-density slice.  Matching attainment on the exact-uniform class remains conditional on the unresolved full-fiber occupancy lift, and the separate adaptation problem remains open with no claimed logarithmic penalty.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman's Theorem~1 gives the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE lower bound on a class requiring the covariate density only to be bounded above.  Their Theorem~2 addresses attainability under separate estimator and design conditions, including additional local-support requirements; the two theorems are not treated here as defining one class.  The present exact-uniform class is a subclass of the common-support/constants Theorem~1 slice: the causal two-fiber constructions prove the dense and sparse privacy lower branches on that subclass, and minimax monotonicity transfers every lower branch upward.  No upper bound is transferred.  Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy motivate conditioning on realized occupancy; Chaudhuri, Loh, Pandey, and Sarkar motivate stable local projections; and Acharya, Sun, and Zhang supply the private Hamming-coupling inequality used in the converse.  Birgé and Asi, Duchi, Haque, Li, and Ruan provide test-selection templates for the unresolved exact-uniform upper construction.  Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel study approximate-private CATE releases rather than this pure-private minimax problem.  Balcer and Vadhan illustrate sparse--dense privacy transitions.  Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen provide templates only for a separate open adaptation question: this note claims neither an adaptive rate nor a logarithmic adaptation penalty.  Gao and Han analyze distinct nonprivate random-design geometry.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The identity in Lemma 2 does not itself solve the full-fiber problem. For arbitrary least-favorable priors, the second-order kernel orientation can depend on a growing nuisance profile, and clipping local projections can reintroduce a sieve-size factor. The proposed early kill test is the finite \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\) two-resolution program from the parent archive: impose every replacement-neighbor constraint, increase both occupancy and nuisance-sign dimension, and reject the route if the optimized weighted-shell functional grows with the nuisance dimension after occupancy weighting.
body.honest_scope: The unconditional results are the occupancy identity, the nonprivate floor, and the dense and sparse pure-private lower branches on the fixed-smoothness exact-uniform class, together with their upward lower-bound transfer to the common-support/constants slice of Kennedy et al.'s Theorem~1 class, whose design density is bounded above but need not be bounded below.  No superclass upper bound is asserted.  The matching upper frontier on the exact-uniform class is explicitly conditional on resolving the full-fiber occupancy lift, and smoothness adaptation is wholly open; no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty is claimed.
